capabilities.title: Choose vLLM vs alternative inference runtimes
capabilities.summary: Decide whether vLLM fits the serving scenario or an alternative runtime is a better match.

when: selecting an inference/serving runtime for an LLM
deploying a production LLM API needing high throughput (100+ req/sec)
serving OpenAI-compatible endpoints or multi-user apps (chatbots, assistants)
serving a large model under limited GPU memory while needing low latency + high throughput
avoid_when: research, prototyping, or one-off generation (prefer HuggingFace transformers)
NVIDIA-only deployment needing absolute maximum performance (consider TensorRT-LLM)
already standardized on the HuggingFace ecosystem (consider Text-Generation-Inference)

expected_outcomes: vLLM delivers up to ~24x higher throughput than standard transformers via PagedAttention (block-based KV cache) and continuous batching
vs TensorRT-LLM on 70B, TRT is ~12% faster but vLLM is far easier to set up and is multi-platform

steps: Use vLLM for production LLM APIs (100+ req/sec), OpenAI-compatible endpoints, multi-user apps, or fitting large models in limited GPU memory with low latency.
Prefer llama.cpp for CPU/edge, single-user inference.
Prefer HuggingFace transformers for research, prototyping, and one-off generation.
Consider TensorRT-LLM only when NVIDIA-only and absolute maximum performance is required.
Consider Text-Generation-Inference when already embedded in the HuggingFace ecosystem.

capabilities.title: Launch an OpenAI-compatible vLLM server sized to the model
capabilities.summary: Start `vllm serve` with flags chosen by model size, then verify readiness before use.

when: serving an LLM behind an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint
deploying a chat/completions API for multiple clients
avoid_when: doing offline batch generation where no server is needed (use the in-process LLM engine)

steps: Install vLLM: `pip install vllm`.
Choose flags by model size: 7B-13B on one GPU -> `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 8192`; 30B-70B -> add `--tensor-parallel-size <power-of-2>` and `--quantization awq`.
For production add `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-metrics --metrics-port 9090 --host 0.0.0.0`.
Start the server, e.g. `vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3-8B-Instruct --port 8000`.
For gated/private models run `huggingface-cli login` first; for custom architectures add `--trust-remote-code`.
Query via the OpenAI SDK against base_url `http://localhost:8000/v1` with api_key `EMPTY`.

validation: A test chat completion via the OpenAI SDK returns non-empty content
recovery: `OSError: MODEL not found` -> verify exact HuggingFace model name/capitalization; run `huggingface-cli login` for gated models; add `--trust-remote-code` for custom models
`Connection refused` when querying -> bind `--host 0.0.0.0`, confirm the port is free with `lsof -i :8000`, and open the firewall
`ImportError: No module named 'flash_attn'` -> `pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation` or launch with `--disable-flash-attn`

capabilities.title: Run offline batch inference with the vLLM engine
capabilities.summary: Generate over many prompts in-process (no HTTP server), letting vLLM batch internally.

when: processing a large dataset of prompts offline
generating outputs for evaluation without server overhead
batch generation inside an ML pipeline
avoid_when: serving live multi-user traffic (use the OpenAI-compatible server)

steps: Load prompts (e.g. one per line from a file) into a list.
Construct `LLM(model=..., tensor_parallel_size=N, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, max_model_len=...)`.
Define `SamplingParams(temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop=[...])`.
Call `llm.generate(prompts, sampling)` ONCE for all prompts — vLLM batches internally; do not manually chunk.
Extract `output.outputs[0].text` and token_ids per result and write to a JSONL file.

validation: Number of output records equals the number of input prompts
Each result contains non-empty generated text

capabilities.title: Select a quantization method (AWQ / GPTQ / FP8)
capabilities.summary: Pick a quantization scheme by GPU type, model size, and accuracy budget.

when: choosing quantization to fit a large model in limited VRAM
deciding between AWQ, GPTQ, and FP8 for serving
avoid_when: sufficient GPU memory is available and best accuracy is required (serve FP16)
model is under 13B parameters with memory to spare

steps: AWQ: 4-bit (~75% compression), <1% accuracy loss, fast — best for 70B production models.
GPTQ: 4-bit, 1-2% loss — widest model support / best compatibility; use when not on H100.
FP8: 8-bit, <0.5% loss, fastest — H100/H800 only (CUDA 12.3+); supports runtime/dynamic quantization with no pre-quantized model.
SqueezeLLM: 3-4 bit extreme compression, 2-3% loss (~96% MMLU on 70B) — verify accuracy before use.
VRAM reference (Llama 2 70B): FP16 ~140GB, FP8 ~70GB, AWQ/GPTQ ~35GB, SqueezeLLM ~26GB.
Prefer pre-quantized HuggingFace models (e.g. `TheBloke/...-AWQ`); quantizing your own needs an 80GB+ GPU and 128-512 diverse calibration samples from the target domain.

capabilities.title: Serve a quantized model to fit limited GPU memory
capabilities.summary: Launch vLLM with a `--quantization` flag matching the model format and verify output quality.

when: a model does not fit in available VRAM at FP16
need to run a 70B model on a single 40GB GPU
avoid_when: adequate VRAM is available and best accuracy is required (serve unquantized)
FP8 is chosen but no H100/H800 GPU is available

steps: Pick a method (see select-quantization-method) and obtain a pre-quantized HF model or use dynamic FP8.
Launch with the matching flag, e.g. `vllm serve TheBloke/Llama-2-70B-AWQ --quantization awq --tensor-parallel-size 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` (fits a 70B model in ~35-40GB VRAM).
The `--quantization` value MUST match the model's format (awq / gptq / fp8).
For FP8 dynamic quantization no pre-quantized model is needed: `vllm serve MODEL --quantization fp8` (H100/H800 only).
Compare quantized outputs against the unquantized model on task-specific prompts to confirm quality.

validation: Server loads without OOM and `curl /health` returns ok
Sampled outputs match expected task quality vs FP16 on representative prompts
recovery: `RuntimeError: Quantization format not supported` -> set `--quantization` to match the model card (awq/gptq)
Poor quality after quantization -> verify config.json quantization_config, try a different method (e.g. FP8 on H100), or serve unquantized
OOM with a quantized model -> ensure the `--quantization` flag is set and try `--dtype float16`

capabilities.title: Resolve vLLM out-of-memory errors
capabilities.summary: Apply the OOM mitigation ladder for model-loading and inference-time CUDA OOM.

when: OOM during inference as the KV cache fills up
model + KV cache exceeds available VRAM
avoid_when: the failure is a correctness/accuracy or connectivity issue rather than memory pressure

steps: Reduce GPU memory utilization: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.7` (try 0.7 / 0.75 / 0.8).
Reduce max sequence length: `--max-model-len 4096` instead of 8192.
Enable quantization for ~4x memory reduction: `--quantization awq`.
Split across GPUs with tensor parallelism (power of 2): `--tensor-parallel-size 2`.
Reduce concurrent sequences: `--max-num-seqs 128` (or 64), and cap per-request `max_tokens` on the client.
For OOM with a quantized model, confirm the `--quantization` flag matches and try `--dtype float16`.

validation: Server loads and serves with no OOM errors in the logs
recovery: OOM persists after lowering utilization -> combine quantization + tensor parallelism + reduced max-model-len
OOM only during inference -> lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` (e.g. 0.85), reduce `--max-num-seqs`, and cap client `max_tokens`

capabilities.title: Tune vLLM throughput and latency
capabilities.summary: Benchmark, then adjust concurrency, caching, and memory utilization to hit throughput/TTFT targets.

when: throughput is below target (<50-100 req/sec) on a working server
avoid_when: the server does not yet start or OOMs at load (resolve memory first)
the problem is output correctness/accuracy rather than performance

expected_outcomes: Prefix caching can cut TTFT substantially for repeated prompt prefixes; speculative decoding yields ~2-3x faster generation for outputs >100 tokens

steps: Measure a baseline: `vllm bench throughput --model MODEL --input-tokens 128 --output-tokens 256 --num-prompts 1000`; record throughput, TTFT, tokens/sec.
Diagnose with `nvidia-smi` (target GPU util >80%) and Prometheus metrics (`curl :9090/metrics | grep vllm`): low GPU util -> under-batched; memory ~100% but GPU <80% -> memory-bound.
For low throughput: raise `--max-num-seqs` (128 -> 256 -> 512) and enable `--enable-prefix-caching`.
For high TTFT: enable `--enable-chunked-prefill`, reduce `--max-model-len`; for long generations use speculative decoding (`--speculative-model DRAFT` or `--speculative-method ngram`).
Tune `--gpu-memory-utilization` (0.7 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95): higher = more batch capacity but higher OOM risk.
Ensure `--tensor-parallel-size` is a power of 2 (4, not 3).
Re-benchmark and compare against targets.

validation: Re-benchmark shows throughput/TTFT moving toward targets (throughput +30-100%, GPU utilization >85%)
recovery: Still <50 req/sec -> increase `--max-num-seqs`, enable prefix caching, confirm GPU util >80%
TTFT still >1s -> enable chunked prefill, reduce `--max-model-len`, or add tensor parallelism to parallelize prefill
OOM after raising utilization/seqs -> lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` to 0.7, reduce `--max-model-len`, or quantize
